newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Kia Group to reduce employees by 3,250.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Kia Group to reduce employees by 3,250.

text.p: South Korea's eighth-largest Kia Group would reduce the number of its employees by 3,250 as part of its plan to restructure its business, a company spokesman said on Friday.
The decision was revealed in a meeting between Kia Group executives and merchant banks on Thursday to explain the group's restructuring programme and to urge lenders to keep credit lines open.
"We will not hire new personnel, if there are some routine vacancies," said the official, declining to elaborate on how the reduction would be achieved.
Local media said Kia Motors would reduce its employees by 2,000, commercial vehicle maker Asia Motors by 300, Kia Steel by 250 and Kisan by 700.
Alarmed by the news, union workers said they would hold a meeting in the afternoon to find out what really happened in the meeting and to discuss counter measures, a union official said.
"We have not yet been informed. We will discuss the issue later today," he said.
The union of Kia Motors on Thursday gave critical support to the group by agreeing to let management set this year's wage increase.
A union leader had said the company had fully explained the company's financial position and asked for the union's understanding.

Kia Group has been battered by rumours of financial troubles for months, leaving lenders reluctant to extend credits, especially in the aftermath of a string of corporate collapses since early this year.
Some financial institutions, especially merchant banks, have tended to shy away from giving loans to the Kia Group.
The spokesman said group vice-chairman Han Seung-jun urged merchant banks at a meeting to maintain credit to the group.
"Kia Group sell cars to 150 countries and has bright export prospects this year," Han was quoted as saying. "We will have no problem if we can overcome the current situation."
An official at the Merchant Banks' Association of Korea said presidents of merchant banks attending the meeting agreed to roll over loans extended to Kia.
"The (merchant bank) representatives shared the opinion that they should cooperate to help keep a sound company afloat," the official said. But he added the agreement had no binding force.
He said some merchant banks had called in loans as they had faced growing financial pressures after some other financial institutions appeared reluctant to buy Kia's discounted commercial papers.
